the_buyer_message.subject: V2.1 shunt controller — 2.7x improvement vs incumbent in computational testing. Bench protocol designed to falsify it. Will your team try to break it?
the_buyer_message.body:
Dear [Name],

We have a control mechanism for multi-segment CSF shunts that shows a 2.7x improvement over existing predictive closed-loop control in our computational testing.

The honest framing:
- 180-run canonical comparison (5 seeds × 9 attacks × 4 arms)
- V2.1 beats the existing published approach (US20210338992A1-style closed-loop) on 9/9 attack modes
- V2.1 wins 5/5 seeds on all 9 attacks
- Ratios range from 1.62x (multi-failure) to 2.85x (fast occlusion)
- This is COMPUTATIONAL evidence, not clinical. We have not built physical hardware.
- One honest weakness: multi-failure (all segments fail) produces catastrophic peak ICP (69.8 mmHg). No controller survives this.

The mechanism is specific: bounded rate of conductance change + sensor-health-aware safe fallback. Not 'AI shunt.' Not 'predictive shunt.' A control regime that remains stable under sensor uncertainty.

We built a complete physical bench protocol specifically designed to FALSIFY our simulator's predictions. 2-arm comparison (existing controller vs V2.1), 80 blinded runs, 4 falsification criteria. If the bench disagrees with our simulator by more than 30%, the simulator is wrong — not the bench.

Cross-domain research confirms: the individual mechanisms (rate limiting, sensor-health fallback) are well-known engineering techniques used in aerospace, robotics, and industrial automation. The novelty is in the specific application to multi-segment hydraulic drainage under physiological sensing constraints.

What I'm asking:
1. Run the simulator on your hardware (Python, no dependencies, 5 minutes)
2. Compare V2.1 to your current approach
3. Try to break V2.1 with your own attack scenarios
4. Tell us: does the rate-limited control + sensor-health fallback mechanism add value beyond your current capability?

If your engineering team says 'this is interesting, send us the bench package' — that's the conversation we want.

If they say 'this doesn't work because ___' — that's also valuable. It enters our evidence loop.

Repository: github.com/prateekm1007/discovery-evidence-fabric
Canonical findings: TTP_PACKAGES/P-01_PROTOTYPE/17_V2_1_canonical_findings.md

Best regards,
[Your name]

miethke_specific_note: Your SENSOR RESERVOIR is the closest existing hardware to what V2.1 needs. You have the sensor. We have the control law. Together = closed-loop adaptive shunt. The bench protocol is designed so your engineering team can build it (~$7-8K, 4-8 weeks) and run 80 blinded runs that either confirm or refute our computational predictions.
